A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions. Internal reporting inconsistencies are identified below.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST training experiments under IID and non-IID partial participation, with and without Byzantine attacks, in Figures 1–6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments, including Byzantine robustness and participation/momentum sweeps, in Figures 1–9 and the experimental appendices.

M1.justification: v1 updates sampled momentum using (1-alpha)m + alpha*g and leaves unsampled caches unchanged. v2 uses (1-alpha_t*p_t)m + alpha_t*r_i*g, decaying every client's cached momentum each round, and introduces preprocessing P for delayed vectors. Section 3.2, Algorithm 1, and Appendix A establish a procedural change beyond renaming D-Byz-SGDM to DeMoA.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates MNIST only; v2 adds CIFAR-10 natural-image classification under IID/non-IID distributions, both with and without Byzantine clients. v2 displays five attack families rather than six, but Tables 2 and 4 still list INF, so missing INF plots do not establish that this attack was no longer evaluated.

E2.justification: The described comparator families remain FedAvg, client-side momentum SGD, and the heuristic momentum extension of Byz-VR-MARINA-PP. FedAvg-M is relabeled and cited as FedCM without a documented procedural difference. The same five aggregators remain, with cp renamed CCLIP. Selecting one tuned MARINA configuration instead of displaying three clipping settings changes protocol/reporting rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: v2 adds p=0.1 and momentum=0.99 settings and a 200-epoch CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 protocol. Benign MNIST changes from learning rate 0.01 to grid search, and displayed loss changes from validation loss to training loss. Both appendices already specify a MNIST ConvNet, despite v1's main-text MLP wording. v2's Byzantine MNIST count conflicts between Section 5.1 (20) and Appendix B/Table 2 (25), preventing a definite count-change inference.

E4.justification: Figures 3–4 add sensitivity comparisons crossing participation rates 0.1/0.5 with momentum values 0.9/0.99. Figures 5–9 extend the per-aggregator robustness analysis to lower participation on MNIST and to CIFAR-10. v1's corresponding experiments used fixed p=0.5 and momentum=0.9. No isolated empirical ablation of the new cache-decay component is provided.

E5.justification: The reported benign seed set changes from {0,1} in v1 Table 1 to {0,1,2} in v2; Byzantine experiments already listed three seeds. v2 explicitly identifies shaded regions as standard deviations across seeds, whereas v1 does not define the shading statistic.

E6.justification: v2 adds CIFAR-10 outcomes and participation/momentum sweep curves and revises MNIST results. For centered-clipping IID ALIE, v1 Figure 1 places the proposed method among the leading curves, whereas v2 Figure 1a clearly places selected Byz-VR-MARINA-PP above DeMoA. INF curves and separate MARINA clipping-setting curves disappear. Algorithm and tuning differences prevent interpreting these replacements as same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v2 removes bounded gradients, changes local smoothness to global smoothness, generalizes heterogeneity to zeta^2+B^2||grad f||^2, and adopts an average-pairwise robust-aggregation definition. Theorem 3.1 and Appendix E replace the earlier analyses with a stated O(c*delta*zeta^2) residual and new G/delta restrictions; Corollary 3.2 adds overparameterization convergence. v1's Omega(delta*zeta^2/p) lower-bound theorem and Appendix G proof are removed. Appendix A adds variance derivations.

C1.justification: The central theoretical contribution changes from claiming an unavoidable, optimally matched 1/p residual penalty to claiming that DeMoA avoids that amplification and converges under overparameterization. The claimed original partial-participation lower-bound contribution disappears. The abstract and conclusion now emphasize low-participation CIFAR-10 robustness and matching existing full-participation guarantees.

C2.justification: v2 adds an implicit-momentum and variance explanation for preprocessing cached updates. It discusses client-count and Byzantine-ratio restrictions and explicitly acknowledges aggregator-dependent failures in Sections 3.3.2 and 5.1, qualifying v1's broad success language. The interpretation of 1/p amplification as unavoidable and the bounded-gradient limitation are withdrawn.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds CIFAR-specific configuration information and explicitly documents selection by highest mean validation accuracy. Hardware, software versions, and the upstream codebase link remain unchanged. v2 omits v1's test batch size, explicit per-client sample counts, and statement that Byzantine clients could access the full training set, producing limited additions and losses in reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 makes MIFA and OrMo central antecedents and explains its claimed differences and inspiration; both works were already cited in v1. It adds implicit-momentum, strong-growth/interpolation, and breakdown/optimality references, including Mitliagkas et al. (2016), Allouah et al. (2023b), and Shi et al. (2025), while pruning many broad FL citations. This substantially revises research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are rewritten with an explicit contribution list; Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 4; assumptions move into Preliminary. The method discussion and Appendix A are extensively reorganized and expanded, the optimizer is renamed DeMoA, proof appendices are restructured, and an Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 becomes a combined MNIST/CIFAR comparison; benign MNIST results move into expanded sweep displays. Plots are redrawn with changed axes, colors, legends, and panel arrangements. The combined configuration table becomes four dataset-specific tables, the notation table disappears, and appendix robustness figures are substantially expanded.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens v1's MNIST-only evidence with CIFAR-10, sensitivity sweeps, and explicit tuning/uncertainty reporting. It also withdraws v1's general 1/p lower-bound claim, whose Appendix G construction imposed an additional restriction on p. However, v2's new variance comparison in Section 3.2/Appendix A.2.2 omits the cached-momentum/gradient cross term, so its asserted variance advantage is not established. MNIST client counts and clipping grids also conflict across passages. These benefits and unresolved weaknesses in the revised scientific justification prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
